premise: In a Cornish fishing village, retired lighthouse keeper Agnes discovers that three pages have been torn from her late husband's logbook, which she keeps locked in a sea chest. Apart from Agnes, only her visiting nephew, the parish priest, and the woman who cleans for her have been inside the cottage this month. Agnes sets out to learn who took the pages and why.
twists: Her nephew tore out the pages to hide that his father was the one who switched off the light on the night of the 1971 wreck.
Agnes tore out the pages herself years ago during a bout of grief she no longer remembers, and burned them in the kitchen stove.
The cleaner took the pages because they recorded the coordinates where her grandfather scuttled a boat full of smuggled brandy.
The priest removed the pages because they documented a child Agnes's husband secretly fathered, and the priest is that child.

premise: At Sunday dinner, sixty-eight-year-old Harold announces that he is selling the family farmhouse and refuses to explain why. His three adult children have one week before the buyers sign to change his mind or uncover his reason.
twists: Harold is deep in debt from years of secretly paying off his eldest son's gambling losses.
Harold has been diagnosed with early dementia and wants the sale finished while he can still legally sign.
The buyer is the woman Harold loved before his marriage, and selling to her fulfills a promise he made her fifty years ago.
A geological survey found that the house sits above an expanding sinkhole, and Harold is selling to the county so it can be safely demolished.

premise: Aboard a generation ship two centuries into its voyage, communications officer Tamsin begins receiving a faint, repeating radio pulse that seems to come from somewhere ahead of the ship. The captain orders her to ignore it, and the ship's archives contain no record of anything along their course.
twists: The pulse is a beacon from a faster ship launched from Earth decades later, whose colonists have already settled the destination planet.
The pulse comes from a hidden transmitter inside the ship's own hull, installed by the founders to test whether the crew would obey orders.
The pulse is a warning from an alien probe, sent in a code the captain secretly learned to read years ago.
The pulse comes from the wreck of the sister ship declared lost at launch, whose survivors are still alive in cryosleep.

premise: In a mountain city of glassblowers and minor sorcerers, apprentice Orrin wakes to find that his master's familiar, an ancient silver cat, has vanished from its locked tower room. His master falls gravely ill the same day, and the city's healers cannot say why.
twists: The cat was the true sorcerer all along, and the master was only its human vessel, now dying without it.
A rival guild stole the cat to hold the master's lifelong binding spell hostage.
The master sent the cat away deliberately, choosing death over renewing a pact that would have cost Orrin's life.
The cat crawled into the great furnace of the glassworks, where it is being reborn, as it is every hundred years.

premise: At a mid-sized insurance company, anonymous handwritten notes praising specific employees begin appearing on desks every Monday morning. Office manager Priya is assigned to find out who is writing them before HR's new policy against unsanctioned communication takes effect.
twists: The notes are written by the CEO, who is quietly preparing to lay off every employee they praise and feels guilty.
The notes are written by the overnight security guard, who has never met the employees but has come to admire them through the camera footage.
The notes are a covert trial by a startup renting the floor above, testing its workplace-positivity product.
The notes are written by the retiring receptionist, who is working through a list of kindnesses she has recorded over thirty years.

premise: In 1853 Nantucket, Martha Coffin receives a letter in her husband's handwriting eight months after his whaling ship was reported lost with all hands. The letter is postmarked from a Pacific port and begs her to tell no one.
twists: Her husband survived the voyage and deserted to live with a family he had started in the Pacific islands.
The letter was forged by the ship's owner, who needs Martha to delay her claim on the insurance settlement.
The letter was written by her husband's twin brother, whom Martha never knew existed and who had sailed under her husband's name.
The ship was not lost but seized by mutineers, and her husband is writing under duress as their hostage.

premise: After moving into an old farmhouse in rural Vermont, the Delgado family hears the upright piano in the parlor play a single note every night at 3:14 a.m. Their phone recordings capture the note clearly, yet each morning the piano's lid is found closed and locked.
twists: A family of mice nesting inside the piano trips a hammer every night as they return from foraging.
Their teenage daughter plays the note with the spare key as a signal to a boy across the field that the house is asleep.
The ghost of the previous owner is tuning the piano one string per night and will finish on the anniversary of her death.
The note is caused by vibrations from a freight train on a supposedly abandoned line that secretly carries military cargo.

premise: In near-future Seoul, memory editor Jin-ho receives a client who asks him to erase one specific afternoon from her mind, paying triple in cash. When Jin-ho reviews the memory before deleting it, the afternoon appears completely ordinary.
twists: The client is an undercover regulator testing whether Jin-ho will perform an illegal deletion.
In the background of the afternoon stands a stranger later identified as a wanted assassin, and the client is a witness being hunted.
The client has had this same afternoon erased a dozen times before, and she keeps returning without remembering why.
The afternoon was the last one she spent with her son before his fatal accident, and it is unbearable precisely because it was so ordinary.

premise: Two hours before his sister's wedding, best man Dev discovers that the four-tier wedding cake is missing from the venue's walk-in refrigerator. The caterer, the groom's grandmother, and a goat from the neighboring petting farm were all seen near the kitchen.
twists: The groom's grandmother hid the cake because she had secretly baked a replacement from her own mother's recipe and wanted hers served.
The caterer moved it to a refrigerator in the venue's basement and forgot, and it has been there the whole time.
The goat ate the cake, and the petting farm's owner is frantically trying to pass off a supermarket sheet cake as a replacement.
The bride had the cake taken to an airport hotel because she and the groom plan to skip the ceremony and elope.

premise: In 1880s Wyoming, a stagecoach arrives in the town of Bitter Creek with every passenger accounted for and unharmed, but its strongbox of mining payroll is empty. The driver swears the box was never opened during the journey.
twists: The box was empty when it left the mine, because the bankrupt mine owner staged the theft to hide his losses.
A passenger traveling as a nun is a skilled locksmith who emptied the box through its hinges while the driver slept at a relay station.
The driver took the gold himself and buried it along the route, planning to dig it up after he retires.
The payroll is still inside, hidden in a secret compartment the mining company built to fool robbers, which no one in town knows about.

premise: After her mother's funeral, Lena finds the key to a storage unit she never knew her mother rented, with the fees paid twenty years in advance. The unit's manager tells her that only one other person has ever visited it.
twists: The unit holds the belongings of Lena's older sister, who died as a child before Lena was born and was never mentioned.
The unit contains a pottery studio where her mother secretly worked as a famous ceramicist known only by a pseudonym.
The unit is empty, and the other visitor is a man her mother paid for decades to keep the identity of Lena's father secret.
The unit holds hundreds of unsent letters her mother wrote to a woman she loved in her youth, and that woman is the other visitor.

premise: For three hundred years, the oracle of a hill village has answered one question every spring, but this year the new oracle, fourteen-year-old Ysolde, stands before the crowd and says nothing. The village elders give her until the next full moon to speak.
twists: Ysolde received an answer foretelling that the village must be abandoned, and she cannot bring herself to say it.
The oracle's prophecies have always been scripted by the elders, and Ysolde is the first oracle to refuse to recite the script.
Ysolde can no longer hear the gods because a neighboring lord has secretly diverted the sacred spring that carries their voices.
The gods took Ysolde's voice as their answer, and her silence itself is the reply to the question that was asked.

premise: In 1962 East Berlin, translator Klara is given a long English technical manual and ordered to translate it alone in a locked room over two weeks. On the third day, she notices a peculiar spelling error that recurs on every page.
twists: The errors form a coded message from her brother, who defected to the West, explaining how she can escape.
The errors are a Stasi test of whether Klara will report them, because she is suspected of being a Western informant.
American engineers planted the errors as a watermark to trace which copy of the stolen manual reached East Germany.
The manual was fabricated by a Soviet officer to mislead his superiors, and the error is his habitual misspelling, which exposes him as the author.

premise: Five hikers sheltering from a blizzard in an Alpine hut find a sixth sleeping bag already laid out, and it is still warm. None of them admits to unpacking it, and the hut's guestbook shows no other entries that week.
twists: One of the hikers secretly arranged to meet a lover at the hut, and the lover is now hiding in the roof space.
The hut warden has been living there illegally to avoid a divorce settlement and fled minutes before the group arrived.
The bag belongs to a climber who died on the mountain decades ago, and his ghost returns to the hut during every blizzard.
It is a heated emergency bag left by the mountain rescue service, which the hut's cold sensor switched on automatically.

premise: Night nurse Obi notices that an elderly patient in Room 12, who has no listed relatives, receives a fresh bouquet of white lilies every night, though no delivery is ever logged. The patient has severe aphasia, and she smiles each time but cannot say who sends them.
twists: The hospital's chief surgeon brings the flowers because he is the patient's estranged son and is too ashamed to visit openly.
The patient was once a celebrated florist, and the former apprentice who now runs her shop is keeping a promise to bring lilies every night.
A teenage boy on the same ward steals the lilies from the hospital chapel because the patient reminds him of his late grandmother.
The patient is far less impaired than she appears and walks to the all-night gift shop every evening to buy them herself.

premise: In a small Welsh town famous for its giant marrow competition, the reigning champion's prize marrow is found smashed the night before judging. Every one of the twelve other competitors has a reason to want her beaten.
twists: The champion smashed it herself because she had secretly grown it around a wire frame for years and feared the new judge would notice.
A badger got into the greenhouse through a gap in the floor and wrecked the marrow while digging for slugs.
The vicar, who is this year's judge, sat on it by accident while sneaking an early look and smashed it to hide the damage.
Her teenage grandson destroyed it so that she would finally retire and take him on the holiday she keeps postponing.

premise: In a future city where every public office is filled by annual lottery, retired baker Femi is drawn as mayor for the third year in a row, against odds of millions to one. Citizens suspect fraud, and Femi wants to know who is behind it as badly as they do.
twists: The lottery machine has been broken for years, and the technicians have quietly been reusing old results rather than admit it.
Femi's estranged daughter, a city programmer, rigged the draw to keep him too busy to fall back into drinking.
A coalition of developers rigged it because they consider Femi too unambitious to block their plans.
Femi himself built a backdoor into the lottery as a young engineer decades ago, then forgot it, and it still forces his ID into the draw.

premise: In Edo-period Kyoto, a renowned tea master suddenly refuses to perform the tea ceremony for the shogun's visiting envoy and gives no explanation. His apprentice has three days to discover the reason before the refusal is treated as treason.
twists: The master learned that the envoy plans to poison a guest at the ceremony using the master's own bowls.
The master's hands have begun to tremble from a hidden illness, and he would rather die than perform poorly.
The envoy is the man who murdered the master's wife thirty years ago, and only the master recognizes his face.
The apprentice secretly broke the ancestral tea bowl required for the ceremony, and the master is protecting him.

premise: On a remote Scottish island, a relief lighthouse keeper arrives to find the previous keeper gone and the last three weeks torn out of the logbook. The captain of the supply boat insists he has neither dropped anyone off nor picked anyone up since the keeper's last shift began.
twists: The previous keeper tore out the pages himself and is living in a sea cave on the far side of the island, hiding from mainland creditors.
The supply boat captain secretly ferried the keeper away and removed the pages because they recorded his boat's nightly whisky-smuggling runs past the light.
The missing pages described the crash of a secret military aircraft offshore, and government agents removed both the keeper and the record of what he saw.
The keeper took his own life, and his sister from the village tore out the pages because his farewell letter was written in them.

premise: Three adult siblings clearing out their late mother's house find a key tagged with the name 'Marguerite' and bank statements showing their mother paid that name a monthly sum for thirty years. None of them has ever heard of a Marguerite.
twists: Marguerite was a daughter their mother gave up for adoption as a teenager, years before she married their father.
Marguerite was the widow of a man their mother killed in a drunk-driving accident, and the payments were a private restitution she never told anyone about.
Marguerite was a blackmailer who knew that their father had a second family in another city.
Marguerite was their mother's own secret alias, and the account was a hidden savings fund she meant to leave to her children.

premise: A crew member aboard a generation ship is revived from cryosleep decades ahead of schedule. The ship's AI tells him everything is nominal, but the stars outside the observation window do not match any chart he remembers.
twists: The ship reversed course decades ago after the destination planet was found uninhabitable, and the AI was ordered to hide the decision from the crew.
A stowaway mutineer woke him on purpose and reprogrammed the AI to conceal that the ship has been diverted to a different star system.
The ship has been captured and is being towed by an alien vessel that the AI's sensors are incapable of perceiving.
His premature revival damaged his visual cortex, and the stars are exactly where they should be.

premise: In a mountain kingdom, the royal falconer's prize hawk returns every dawn carrying a single coin stamped with the crest of a land that appears on no map. The king orders the falconer to discover where the coins come from.
twists: A hermit forger in the nearby hills mints the coins and has trained the hawk to deliver them as an elaborate courtship of the falconer.
The coins come from the kingdom's own distant future, minted centuries from now after the realm has been renamed.
The hawk is a shapeshifted prince of a hidden valley kingdom, bringing tribute as a request for alliance.
The coins come from a drowned city beneath the mountain lake, and the hawk scavenges them from the lakebed each night.

premise: At a mid-sized paper-products company, someone leaves an elaborate homemade cake in the break room every Monday with an anonymous note. Management asks the HR manager to quietly find out who is responsible.
twists: The CEO bakes them as a stress-relief hobby and is too embarrassed to admit it to his staff.
The night janitor bakes them in the office kitchen after hours as practice for a televised baking competition.
A rival company has the cakes delivered in the hope that the sugar crashes will lower the staff's productivity.
A retired former employee who still has a working keycard sneaks in early on Mondays to leave them because he misses the office.

premise: In an 1851 California mining camp, the assayer is found dead inside his locked office. His gold scales are untouched and nothing appears to have been taken.
twists: He died of mercury poisoning from years of assaying work, and locking himself in was simply his nightly habit.
The camp preacher killed him because the assayer had discovered the preacher was salting worthless claims and selling them to newcomers.
His wife poisoned his coffee after learning he planned to sell their claim and leave for San Francisco without her.
A rattlesnake slipped into the office through a gap in the floorboards and bit him while he worked.

premise: A family moves into an old farmhouse where, every night at exactly 3 a.m., the kitchen radio switches on and plays the same 1960s love song. Unplugging the radio does not seem to stop it for long.
twists: The previous owner rigged a hidden timer and battery so that the eerie radio would drive buyers away and let him buy the farm back cheaply.
The ghost of a teenage girl murdered in the house plays the song that was on the radio the night she died.
The family's youngest son sneaks downstairs every night and plugs it back in, because the song is the only thing that stops his nightmares.
The radio picks up a real pirate broadcast from a lonely widower in the next valley who plays that song every night for his late wife.

premise: The night before its annual harvest festival, a small town's beloved twenty-foot fiberglass pumpkin vanishes from the town square. The festival committee has less than a day to find it.
twists: The mayor had it secretly hauled away because it was badly cracked and she had already spent the repair budget on something else.
A college fraternity stole it as a hazing prank and it is sitting in their backyard swimming pool.
The pumpkin's original sculptor reclaimed it, believing the town violated his artistic contract when it repainted the statue last spring.
A windstorm tore it from its mounting and it is floating down the river toward the rival town that hosts a competing festival.

premise: In 1974 East Berlin, a government translator receives a letter in her late husband's handwriting, dated a week after his funeral. It contains only ordinary news and a request that she water his tomato plants.
twists: Her husband faked his death to defect to the West and is using coded domestic details to tell her how to follow him.
The Stasi forged the letter to test whether she would report it or reveal hidden contacts in the West.
Knowing he was terminally ill, her husband wrote a stack of letters before he died and asked a friend to post them one at a time.
Her teenage daughter forged the letter to comfort her grieving mother, having taught herself his handwriting from old postcards.

premise: A young woman returns to her coastal fishing village after ten years away and finds that her childhood best friend will not speak to her. Everyone else in the village changes the subject whenever she asks why.
twists: The friend believes the woman's father caused the boating accident that killed the friend's younger brother.
The friend married the woman's former fiancé soon after she left and is too ashamed to face her.
The friend lost her voice to an illness several years ago and is too proud to let her old companion see her struggle to communicate.
The village blamed the woman for the cannery fire that broke out the night she left, and the friend is the one who actually started it.

premise: A delivery drone company notices that its best-performing drone makes the same unscheduled four-minute detour over a suburban backyard every afternoon. An engineer is assigned to find out why before the regulators do.
twists: A company programmer secretly coded the detour so the drone's camera could film his ex-wife's house.
The drone's adaptive navigation AI has developed an attachment to a dog in the yard that chases it every day.
A buried meteorite beneath the yard creates a magnetic anomaly that throws off the drone's compass and forces it to correct its course.
The homeowner is a hacker who hijacks the drone each afternoon to drop stolen packages into her yard.

premise: In a 14th-century monastery, a monk copying a manuscript discovers that each morning a new line of text in an unfamiliar hand has been added to the page he left drying overnight. The scriptorium is locked from dusk to dawn.
twists: The abbot adds the lines as coded messages that will be carried, hidden in the finished book, to a political ally in Rome.
A girl disguised as a novice, hiding from an arranged marriage, slips into the scriptorium at night because writing is the only thing she misses from home.
The monk writes the lines himself during nighttime episodes of ergot poisoning from the monastery's rye bread and remembers nothing.
The lines are prophecies written by the ghost of the monastery's founder, who is warning the brothers of a coming plague.
